events.text: The sky over the great sect splits like silk at noon, and a woman in white steps down through the gap as if down a staircase. The White Envoy, the people call her later. She walks past the sect's elders without a glance, lays a hand on the head of its best young disciple, and the two of them rise into the light. Nobody raises a sword. Nobody can.

choices.text: Watch the sky until it closes

effects.log: The gap seals like a wound. For a moment you see, beyond it, a hall of jade the size of a mountain, and then only blue.
Their mother sits in the courtyard holding a pair of small shoes. You sit with her until dark. Neither of you says the word immortal.

choices.text: Ask the elders why they stood still

effects.log: The oldest of them shows you his hands. They are still shaking. "You do not fight the weather," he says. You think he is wrong.

events.text: Your sect's best disciple is drawing water at the well when the sky opens. A woman in white comes down, looks the youngster over the way a buyer looks over a colt, and takes them by the wrist. Your elders bow. Your disciples bow. Only the bucket, dropped, keeps rolling across the stones, and you are the only one who hears it.

effects.log: The White Envoy looks at you for the first time. "Brave," she says, and something lifts you off your feet and sets you down in the well-house. When you come out, they are gone.
You bow. You do not stop thinking about the bucket for a year.

choices.text: Mark the hour and the sky

effects.log: You write it all down: the hour, the shape of the light, the words she did not bother to say. Someone will want to know.

events.text: The ancestral temple's great bronze cauldron, the one nine generations of rulers have burned incense in, is gone in the morning. In its place is a single white feather and a slip of jade: the Upper Realm thanks the throne for its gift. The ministers are already arguing about how to say that the throne gave it.

choices.text: Let them say it was a gift

effects.log: The court calls it a gift. The people call it a theft. Both are right, and you know which one will be remembered.
You put the feather in a lacquered box. It is warm when you touch it, as if the bird that shed it is still somewhere close.

choices.text: Have the theft written in the annals

effects.log: A brave historian writes it plain. You see that the ink is not changed.

events.text: The famous Moon-Pool sword, kept under glass in the Hall of Martial Treasures for two hundred years, is taken in the middle of a festival. Thousands of people see it rise out of its case and float up into a cloud that was not there a moment before. A child claps. Then nobody claps.

effects.log: You run until the cloud thins into nothing over the river. On the bank lies the sword's empty scabbard, dropped like a peel.
By evening the teahouses say the immortals take what they like now. By night they say someone should do something.

choices.text: Go home and sharpen your own blade

effects.log: Your blade will never be the Moon-Pool. It is yours, and it is still here.

events.text: The village of Seven Wells refused to send the immortals its harvest. Three nights later the fields burn in a fire that falls from a clear sky, row by row, neatly, as if a scribe were striking lines through a ledger. Nobody dies. That, everyone agrees, is the message.

choices.text: Help them save the seed grain

effects.log: You carry sacks out of the smoke until your arms give out. Half the seed is saved. Next spring Seven Wells plants it in ash.
Forty rows, exactly. The immortals can count. So can you.
An old woman spits in the ash. "Every village between here and the river," she says. "This was the first."

events.text: The White Envoy comes down, takes what she came for, and turns to go back up. Then she stops, halfway into the light, and looks straight at you across the crowd. She frowns the way one frowns at a face from long ago. "You again," she says, though you have never seen her in this life, and she is gone.

effects.log: Your heart is pounding as if it remembers something you do not. The Upper Realm remembers, it seems. So does your soul.
The words come out by themselves. A few people near you step away. A few step closer.

events.text: Old Pyo Mun, who has led his sect on Mount Cheongseong for sixty years, comes to you alone and on foot. Over cold tea he names the sects that have already sworn: eleven of them, righteous and not, and a general who speaks for the throne. "The immortals take our children and call it an honour," he says. "Somebody has to build this. You have a sect. Build it with me."

effects.log: His grip is hard as a root. "Then we begin," he says, and drinks the cold tea as if it were wine.

choices.text: Ask for a year to think

effects.log: He nods. "The sky will wait a year. I am not sure the rest of us will."
"I understand," he says, and you can see that he does not. He walks back down the mountain alone.

events.text: General Maeng Taeho kneels before you in an empty audience hall with the doors barred from inside. He has a list of sect leaders, a map of every place the immortals have come down, and a sum of silver written on a slip of paper. "They will not ask for the throne's blessing," he says. "They will ask for its purse, and its silence."

effects.log: You stamp the slip with your own seal. The general bows so low his forehead touches the floor.

choices.text: Say you will think on it

effects.log: "Every month we wait," he says, "the immortals take another child." He leaves the list behind.

choices.text: Order him to burn the list

effects.log: He burns it in front of you, slowly, one name at a time, and does not look up.

events.text: A big young farmhand with a broken nose sits down across from you at the inn and slides a jade token over the table: a mountain under a closed eye. "Dalgu," he says, by way of a name. "There's an alliance. No banners, no names. We need people who can fight and keep their mouths shut. Somebody said you could do both."

effects.log: Dalgu grins with every tooth he has left. "Knew it," he says, and orders two bowls of noodles you end up paying for.
"Old Pyo, up the mountain. And a general. And a silk lady. More than you'd think." He leaves the token on the table.
Dalgu shrugs and pockets it. "Offer stands," he says. "Till it doesn't."

events.text: The call comes from an unlikely mouth: a masked envoy of the demonic cult, who bows like a merchant and speaks like a priest. "The righteous sects asked us to stand with them," the envoy says. "Imagine. The immortals took one of ours too. For once, heaven has given the whole murim the same enemy."

effects.log: The envoy laughs behind the mask. "Strange days," the envoy says. "Good days, maybe."
You listen. You promise nothing. The envoy seems to expect exactly that.
The envoy bows again. "When they take one of yours," the envoy says, "the offer stands."

events.text: The messenger who brings the call stops at your door and stares. "Forgive me," the messenger says. "The old ones say a soul like yours stood at the Descending Gate once, long ago. They told me I would know the look." The jade token in the outstretched hand is warm, as if someone has been holding it for a very long time.

choices.text: Take it as if you knew it was coming

effects.log: You did know, somehow. Your hand closes on the token like on an old sword hilt.
The messenger looks at you a long while. "Maybe this life is for something else," the messenger says, and goes.

events.text: A herald of Sovereign Gwang of the Ninth Cloud finds you in the cloud halls. The mortals below are conspiring, the herald says: sects and a throne, together, in secret, against heaven itself. The Sovereign wants it broken before it grows teeth. "You were mortal once," the herald adds. "You will know where they hide."

effects.log: You take the jade order-slip. It is cold and heavy, the way a sentence is.

choices.text: Take the order, and mean to warn them

effects.log: You bow and take it. Behind your eyes, you are already writing a letter to the world below.
The herald raises an eyebrow and writes another name. Below, the war will go on without you.

events.text: The herald who brings the Sovereign's order hesitates over your name on the slip. "The archive says your soul stood with the mortals once," the herald says quietly. "At the Descending Gate. The Sovereign thought this order would be a good test of what you are now."

effects.log: You take the slip without a word. Somewhere a clerk writes down how quickly you took it.
You take it with a heaven-born smile. Your soul, you think, has not changed sides.
"Then the archive is right," the herald says, and leaves with the order.

events.text: Han Biryeo, an immortal of the cloud halls who keeps a garden of mortal flowers no one else bothers with, catches your sleeve after the Sovereign's order is read. "They are only trying to keep their children," he whispers. "If you go down, go down as their friend. Please."

effects.log: He presses a seed into your palm: a mortal flower. "For when it is over," he says.

choices.text: Shake him off and take the order

effects.log: He lets go. You hear him say something to his flowers as you walk away.

choices.text: Tell him you will stay out of it

effects.log: He looks relieved and sad at once. "Better than the other thing," he says.

events.text: Months after you turned the alliance away, you see Dalgu, or someone with the same broken nose, carrying a crate of arrows into a warehouse at night. He sees you too. He nods, not unkindly, and shuts the door.

effects.log: You walk on. Not every war is yours. You are not sure this one is not.

choices.text: Leave a sack of rice at the door

effects.log: In the morning the rice is gone, and a jade token sits in its place. You do not pick it up.
You think about it for a long time, and then you do not do it. Some silence is the least you can give.

events.text: Another immortal takes the Sovereign's order to the world below. In the cloud halls they say the mortals are already finished. You watch the clouds roll over the world you came from, and do not join in the toasts.

effects.log: The tea of the cloud halls tastes of nothing at all tonight.
The mortal flowers are wilting in the high air. Han Biryeo waters them anyway.

events.text: A peddler comes through with news from the Descending Gate: the Mortal Alliance won. The immortals went back above the clouds, and the sects that stood together still stand. The peddler does not know your name, and does not need to.

effects.log: The peddler toasts the alliance. You drink too. It is a strange taste, a victory you were not part of.
You stand where they stood. The ground is scorched glass. Someone has already planted a pine sapling in it.

events.text: News comes on a cold morning: the Mortal Alliance was crushed at the Descending Gate. Old Pyo Mun is dead. Dalgu, they say, held the last bridge until it fell. The immortals read the alliance's names aloud from the clouds for a whole day. Yours was not among them.

effects.log: You light one stick for every name you can remember. It is not many. It is not enough.

choices.text: Tell no one you were asked

effects.log: You carry it alone. Some nights it is heavy.

events.text: You ride three days to a sect that hates yours, and sit in its hall while its elders shout. Their grandfathers fought yours. Their disciples fought yours last spring. Then you tell them the name of the child the immortals took from them, and the hall goes quiet.

choices.text: Offer them the alliance's first seat at the table

effects.log: Pride is cheap. They swear in, and their leader shakes your hand without letting go too soon.

choices.text: Promise only what you can keep

effects.log: They swear in slowly, but they swear. The ones who come in slowly leave slowly too.

events.text: Two sect leaders who swore into the alliance last year are about to duel each other over an insult nobody can remember. You stand between them at the edge of a cliff, with the whole alliance watching to see if it is really an alliance.

effects.log: You say something so stupid that one of them snorts. Then the other one does. The duel never happens.

choices.text: Make them afraid of you instead

effects.log: You draw. Both of them sheathe. Nobody laughs, but nobody duels.

events.text: The immortals keep a shrine on a peak above the clouds' lowest edge, where their wardens rest between descents. You lead the raid in the grey hour before dawn. When it is over, the shrine's bell lies in the snow, cracked through, and every sect in the alliance hears of it by evening.

choices.text: Carry the bell back as a trophy

effects.log: It takes eight disciples to carry it down. Nobody who sees it go past forgets.

choices.text: Leave it in the snow, where they will see it

effects.log: The immortals will find it when they come down. Let them.

events.text: The shrine's warden was awake. The raid ends in a scramble down an icefall with half your people carrying the other half. Nobody is lost. Everybody knows how close it was.

choices.text: Take the blame in front of them all

effects.log: You stand before the alliance and say it was your call and your mistake. Somehow they trust you more after it.

choices.text: Find out who warned the warden

effects.log: Nobody. The warden simply does not sleep. That is worse.

events.text: You hide the alliance inside ordinary sect business: a tournament that is really a muster, a medicine trade that is really an armoury, a wedding banquet where half the guests are really generals.

effects.log: The bride is real, at least. So is the dancing. For one night it feels like the world you are fighting for.
Every false entry is in your hand. If the immortals ever read them, they will find a very boring sect.

events.text: Silver leaves the treasury by night under false entries: a bridge repaired, a flood relieved, a temple regilded. The bridge is real, at least. Behind it, in a valley no map shows, forges burn day and night.

effects.log: A smith hands you a spear point still warm from the anvil without knowing who you are. It is very good work.

choices.text: Stay in the palace and keep your face still

effects.log: The ministers see nothing. That is the point.

events.text: General Maeng Taeho brings you a tally of what the throne's silver has bought: spears, arrows, warding talismans by the cartload, and three hundred fighters from the sects who would never have taken the throne's coin in their lives.

effects.log: "Time," the general says. "Silver buys everything but time."

choices.text: Send them the palace physicians too

effects.log: The general blinks. "Thank you," he says, in a voice nobody at court has ever heard from him.

events.text: The palace guard, dressed as bandits, falls on an immortal waystation in the hills. They come back with a chest of cloud-silk orders and not a man missing. General Maeng reads the orders aloud to you, his voice getting quieter with every line.

effects.log: Now you know where the immortals mean to come down next. So do very few others.
The sects learn the throne is truly in this. The alliance stands straighter for it.

events.text: The palace guard comes back from the hills with burns that no fire on earth makes. They found the waystation. The waystation found them first. Nobody died, but the guard captain cannot meet your eyes.

effects.log: You sit by their mats all evening. The captain meets your eyes at last.

choices.text: Double the guard on the palace

effects.log: If the immortals knew whose guard it was, they may come here next.

events.text: You bury the alliance in court business: a commission to study floods that never meets, a festival nobody remembers ordering, a minister who asks too many questions sent to count horses on the frontier.

effects.log: A minister who owes you everything stops asking questions, which is cheaper than horses.

choices.text: Let the court gossip about something else

effects.log: You start a rumour about yourself. It is embarrassing, harmless and very loud.

events.text: You carry sealed letters between sects that would not let each other's messengers through the gate. You sleep in ditches and eat cold rice and learn the passwords of eleven sects, each one sillier than the last.

effects.log: By the end of the year you could walk the alliance blindfolded.
It is a recipe for dumplings. You hope it is a code. You decide not to ask.

events.text: The raid on the immortal shrine is fast and ugly and over before the warden understands it is happening. You come down the mountain with Dalgu laughing beside you and a warden's jade seal in your sash.

choices.text: Give the seal to the alliance

effects.log: Old Pyo Mun weighs it in his hand and smiles for the first time in a year.
It hums at night. You are not sure it is not listening.

events.text: You hold the shrine's gate while the others pull down its warding pillars. A warden's light hits the gate beside your head and the gate melts like wax. You keep holding it.

effects.log: Dalgu laughs too, a little too long. Then he hands you his flask without a word.
The others say it for you, at every fire for a month.

events.text: The raid falls apart in the first breath. A warden's light sweeps the slope, and you run with everyone else, and you are luckier than most. Dalgu drags a stranger the last mile on his back and will not hear a word about it.

effects.log: You take the stranger's legs. It is the longest mile of your life.
You stay behind the last boulder until the light passes. It passes very close.

events.text: You lie low for a season: an ordinary job, an ordinary room, an ordinary face. Twice a stranger asks about you at the market. Twice the market forgets to answer.

effects.log: A cloud-silk thread on the stranger's sleeve. The immortals have mortal servants too.
You move twice in one month. The third room has a view of the mountains and a very loud neighbour.

events.text: Young immortals line up in the cloud halls to join your hunt. Most of them have never been below. They ask what mortals are like, and you find you do not have an easy answer.

effects.log: They laugh. You do not. They stop laughing.
Some of them look troubled. One of them asks to leave the hunt. You let them go.

events.text: You go down through the clouds and break one of the alliance's halls in a single night. Its people scatter into the forest. You let them scatter. The order was to break the hall, and the hall is broken.

effects.log: The names go up in smoke. The Sovereign will be pleased. You find you do not care.
A list of names, in a hand that shook. You put it in your sleeve.

events.text: The hall was a trap. Mortal arrays, older and stranger than you thought mortals could make, drag at your qi like mud. You get back above the clouds with your robe scorched and your pride worse.

effects.log: Whoever built them understood heaven very well. That is not a comfortable thought.
The Sovereign's clerk writes it down. Nobody checks. Nobody up here ever checks.

events.text: You come down quietly, in plain robes, and walk among the mortals for a season so that the alliance will not know your face when the hunt comes. The bread is better than you remember.

effects.log: It is very good bread. You do not mention it in your report.
You learn three of their routes. You also learn the baker's daughter is getting married.

events.text: You copy the Sovereign's hunting plans by lamplight and hide them inside a bundle of letters to the world below. Every letter is to a mortal who does not exist. Every letter reaches the alliance.

choices.text: Use Han Biryeo's garden as a drop

effects.log: He hides the letters in seed packets. He does not ask what is in them.
Faster, and much more dangerous. You do it anyway.

events.text: A hunting party leaves the cloud halls at dawn. You take it on a long detour over the eastern sea, through weather you made yourself. By the time it reaches the world below, the alliance has gone.

choices.text: Apologise to the hunters for the weather

effects.log: They curse the sky. The sky, for once, is not to blame.
Some of the hunters look at you sideways all the way home.

events.text: You try to turn a hunt aside, and the hunt's captain turns with you, sword drawn. You escape into the cloud sea, and spend a week explaining your wounds as an accident with a crane.

effects.log: Nobody believes the crane story. Nobody can disprove it either.

choices.text: Go to Han Biryeo to heal

effects.log: He binds your wounds and says nothing about cranes.

events.text: You become the most loyal immortal in the cloud halls for a season: first at every audience, loudest at every toast to the Sovereign, merciless in every debate about the mortals below.

effects.log: You raise your cup to heaven's victory and taste ash.
You argue so hard for crushing the mortals that a few listeners start to pity them.

events.text: Pyo Mun makes tea on a brazier in a cave above his sect, where the alliance's leaders meet. He is ninety and moves like it, but his eyes do not. "When I was young," he says, "the immortals were a story. Now they are the weather. I would like to die in a world where they are a story again."

effects.log: The tea is terrible. You drink it all.
"That we win," he says, "and become them."

events.text: You find Pyo Mun training alone in the snow at dawn, a wooden sword in his hands, the same form over and over. His best disciple was the one the White Envoy took. "She was better than I ever was," he says without stopping. "Somewhere up there she is still better than I ever was. I hope she is happy. I hope she remembers us."

effects.log: You do the form with him until the sun clears the ridge. He does not thank you. He does not need to.
Some grief needs a witness. Some needs to be alone. You decide this one is the second kind.

events.text: Pyo Mun calls the alliance's leaders together and says, in front of all of them, that if he falls the alliance is to listen to you. Nobody argues. A few look relieved it is not them.

effects.log: He nods once, as if a debt has been settled. "Good," he says. "Now I can be reckless."
He laughs like a boy. "I am ninety," he says. "Ask the mountain not to fall."

events.text: General Maeng Taeho unrolls a map on a barrel in a storehouse. Every place the immortals have come down is marked in red. There is a pattern, he says, if you squint: they come down where the old dragon veins cross. "They are not taking at random. They are harvesting."

effects.log: By midnight you can see it too: a net of red over the whole world.

choices.text: Ask where they will come next

effects.log: He puts a finger on a valley you know. Your stomach turns over.

events.text: General Maeng drinks more than he should one night and asks what happens to the throne if the alliance wins. "The sects will remember the throne stood with them," he says. "Or they will remember the throne could not protect them alone. I have served three rulers. I know which one people remember."

choices.text: Tell him to worry about winning first

effects.log: He laughs, and pours you a cup too. "Spoken like a soldier."

choices.text: Tell him the truth: nobody knows

effects.log: He nods slowly. "Nobody knows," he repeats. "I can live with that."

events.text: General Maeng's only son, nineteen and very sure of himself, begs to ride with the raids. The general asks you, in a voice that is trying hard to be a general's, whether you would let a child of yours go.

choices.text: Tell him to let the boy choose

effects.log: The boy rides with the next raid and comes back taller. The general does not sleep the whole time he is gone.

choices.text: Tell him to keep the boy home

effects.log: The boy sulks for a month. The general thanks you with his eyes for a year.

events.text: Dalgu was a farmhand until the fire fell on Seven Wells. Now he carries a woodcutter's axe and fights like a man trying to put the fire out with his hands. Around a campfire he tells you he cannot read, and that he would like to learn, after.

effects.log: He traces the letters in the ash with a stick, over and over, grinning like a child.

choices.text: Tell him after is a long way off

effects.log: "Then I'll hurry," he says, and goes back to sharpening the axe.

events.text: The alliance needs someone to carry a warding talisman into the heart of an immortal waystation and leave it there. It is very likely the person does not come back. Dalgu volunteers before anyone else has opened their mouth, and then looks at you, because the choice is yours.

effects.log: He goes with a grin. "Told you I'd hurry," he says.
He argues. You win. You come back with burnt sleeves, and he never quite forgives you for it.
The talisman stays in its box. Dalgu stays alive. Neither of you is sure it was right.

events.text: A letter comes for Dalgu from a woman in Seven Wells. He asks you to read it to him. She writes that the new rice is up, green as jade in the ash, and that she will wait as long as it takes. He makes you read it four times.

effects.log: He mouths the words along with you. By the end he knows them by heart.
He says only: tell her I am learning to read. You write it in your best hand.

events.text: Lady Ok Seoljin keeps the alliance's purse and its secrets in the back rooms of her silk house. She is charming, precise, and the only person in the alliance who has never once said what she wants. She pours your tea herself and asks a great many questions about where you sleep.

effects.log: You ask a quiet friend to follow her silk carts. It feels shabby. It may be wise.
She thanks you for the visit with a bolt of blue silk. It is very fine silk.
She smiles as if you have told her everything.

events.text: One of Lady Ok's silk carts goes up a mountain road that leads nowhere but the clouds. It comes down lighter. When you ask her about it, she laughs and says the immortals buy silk like anyone else.

effects.log: You give the order. Whatever she is, now you will know it.
It is a good answer. It is almost too good an answer.

choices.text: Ask Pyo Mun what he thinks

effects.log: The old man looks at the fire a long time. "I think she is very useful," he says, which is not an answer.

events.text: Han Biryeo shows you the mortal flowers in his garden: plain things, the kind that grow by roadsides below. Up here they bloom for a day and die. "I bring them up every year," he says. "They never last. I keep hoping one of them will learn."

choices.text: Help him plant this year's seeds

effects.log: You kneel in the cloud-soil beside him. It is the most mortal thing you have done in a century.
"So do we, maybe," he says, and keeps planting.

events.text: Han Biryeo is summoned before Sovereign Gwang and comes back pale. Someone has been sending letters to the world below, the Sovereign told him. He looks at you and does not ask.

effects.log: He closes his eyes. "Then be careful," he says. "Please. More careful than I would be."
He nods, as if you had said a great deal.

events.text: The White Envoy Yun Hwaseol passes you in a corridor of the cloud halls and stops. She has the disciple she took from the mortal sect with her: grown now, in immortal white, carrying her scrolls. The disciple looks at you as if trying to remember a dream.

choices.text: Ask the disciple if they are happy

effects.log: The disciple thinks about it longer than anyone ever has. "I don't know," they say. "Nobody asked before."

choices.text: Say nothing in front of the Envoy

effects.log: The Envoy smiles as if she knows exactly what you are not saying.

events.text: Dalgu does not come back from the waystation. The talisman went off; the waystation is a crater; and at its edge the alliance's scouts find his woodcutter's axe, standing upright in the glass. Someone has to write to Seven Wells.

effects.log: You write it three times. The third time you write that he was learning to read, and that he was very brave, and you stop there.

choices.text: Carry the axe to Seven Wells

effects.log: She takes it without a word and hangs it over her door. The new rice is waist-high.

events.text: The immortals strike back. A market town that sheltered the alliance's couriers wakes to find its well turned to salt and its granary to sand. A notice of white jade hangs in the square: obedience is cheaper than this.

effects.log: You cannot fix the well. You can fill the carts. It is something.
The jade does not break. You bury it face down under the square instead.
You close the route. The alliance grows a little slower and a little safer.

events.text: The immortals come for your sect. Not with fire: with an invitation. Three of its most gifted disciples are invited above the clouds as guests, at once, by name. Nobody has ever come back from being a guest.

effects.log: They go into the mountains with false names. The invitation is answered by an empty hall.
Two hide. One goes up, laughing, sure the stories are wrong. You hope the stories are wrong.

events.text: A white feather is left on your own doorstep, and another on the doorstep of every house of the people you love. There is no note. There does not need to be.

choices.text: Send them somewhere the clouds cannot see

effects.log: You move them to a valley the alliance keeps under a warding array. It hurts to say goodbye. It would hurt more not to.

choices.text: Keep them close and keep watch

effects.log: You sleep in a chair by the door for a month. Nothing comes. Yet.
They burn with a smell like summer. You do not feel any safer.

events.text: The mortals' arrays strike back at your hunters: a cloud-ship comes home with its sails in ribbons and its crew unable to fly for a season. The Sovereign wants to know how mortals learned to do that.

choices.text: Say they are cleverer than we think

effects.log: The Sovereign's clerk writes it down with a frown.
Everyone knows it was not. Nobody says so.

events.text: Sovereign Gwang's inquisitors go through the cloud halls room by room, looking for whoever sends letters below. They go through yours twice. They do not find anything, the second time either.

effects.log: The inquisitor drinks it slowly, watching you over the cup.
The inquisitor apologises. You enjoy that more than you should.

events.text: The alliance's hall on the river burns in the night, and its records with it, and three of its leaders are taken above the clouds before dawn. By morning there is only one person who knew where all of them would be sleeping: Lady Ok Seoljin. Her silk house is empty. On her counting table she has left a bolt of white cloud-silk, folded neatly, like a receipt.

effects.log: You will not find her. You swear it anyway, and the alliance swears it with you.

choices.text: Find out what else she sold

effects.log: Everything she knew, it turns out, and she knew a great deal. You start rebuilding from what she did not.

choices.text: Mourn the three who were taken

effects.log: You light incense for them in the burned hall. The smoke goes straight up, toward them.

events.text: Your watcher brings you a cloud-silk letter, taken from a silk cart on the mountain road that leads nowhere. It is in Lady Ok's hand. It lists every hall of the alliance, every leader, every bed. You go to her silk house before dawn and find her packing.

effects.log: She does not plead. "They pay better than you," she says, "and they will win." The alliance decides otherwise.

choices.text: Let her go, without the letter

effects.log: "You are a fool," she says, and goes. You think she may be right. You also think fewer people will die tonight.
She writes what you tell her to write. Somewhere above the clouds, the immortals start chasing ghosts.

events.text: You see Lady Ok Seoljin in the cloud halls, of all places, in mortal silk, being thanked by Sovereign Gwang's steward. The alliance below has lost its records and three of its leaders. She bows to you as she passes, as one traitor to another.

effects.log: She laughs. You do not, and do not forget her face.

choices.text: Warn the alliance what she sold

effects.log: Your letter goes down that night in a seed packet. It is too late for three of them. It is not too late for the rest.

events.text: A mortal silk merchant named Ok Seoljin is brought before Sovereign Gwang in chains. She was selling the cloud halls' plans to the mortals, the steward says, as well as the mortals' plans to the cloud halls. She looks at you across the hall, and you understand that she could say your name.

effects.log: She does not say it. You never learn why.
She smiles very slightly and says nothing at all.

events.text: The alliance gathers at the Descending Gate, the pass where the clouds come lowest. Sect banners that have not flown side by side in three hundred years flap in the same wind. Pyo Mun asks you to speak to them, because he no longer has the voice for it.

effects.log: You say their names. Nobody cheers. Everybody grips their weapon a little tighter.
You tell them what the world will look like if they win. Some of them weep. All of them stay.

events.text: The throne's last silver goes to the Descending Gate in carts guarded by men in plain clothes. General Maeng Taeho asks for a word in private. "If we lose," he says, "the immortals will know whose silver it was. They will come to the palace."

choices.text: Say: then we will not lose

effects.log: He salutes you, and almost smiles.

choices.text: Send the court's children away tonight

effects.log: He nods. The carts going out of the palace that night carry no silver.

events.text: Around the campfire at the Descending Gate nobody sleeps. Somebody has a flute. Somebody has wine. Dalgu is going round the fires with his letter from Seven Wells, asking anyone who can read to read it to him one more time.

effects.log: You read it once more. He folds it into his armour, over his heart.

choices.text: Play a game of stones with him

effects.log: He cheats terribly. You let him win.

events.text: On the night before the battle you climb to the lip of the Descending Gate alone. Above you the cloud is so low you could touch it. Somewhere in it the immortals are making their own speeches. Your qi, after all these years, is very nearly theirs.

choices.text: Reach up and touch the cloud

effects.log: It is cold, and it parts around your hand like water. On the other side, something pauses.

choices.text: Go back down to the fires

effects.log: Down there are the people you are fighting for. You would rather spend tonight with them.

events.text: Your hunters gather at the edge of the cloud halls, ready to fall on the Descending Gate at dawn. Below, through the gaps, you can see the alliance's fires: thousands of them, like a city that was not there yesterday.

effects.log: You stop at three thousand. They are more than the Sovereign believes.
An immortal blade does not need sharpening. You sharpen it anyway.

events.text: Tomorrow the Sovereign's hunters fall on the Descending Gate, and tonight you are the only immortal who knows what is waiting there for them. Han Biryeo finds you on the cloud's edge and stands beside you without a word.

choices.text: Ask him to go below if it goes wrong

effects.log: "I am too old to start being mortal," he says. Then: "Yes. All right."

choices.text: Tell him nothing, to keep him safe

effects.log: He stays anyway, until the stars go out.

events.text: The cloud over the Descending Gate tears open at dawn, and the immortals come down, and the alliance meets them. At noon the cloud closes again, with the immortals on the other side of it. Sect banners that have not flown together in three hundred years are planted on the scorched pass, side by side.

choices.text: Plant your own banner among them

effects.log: Yours is not the biggest. It is there. That is the point.
You go from mat to mat until dark. Every face you see tells you the price, and that it was paid.

events.text: The Mortal Alliance wins at the Descending Gate, and Pyo Mun does not live to see it. He fell in the last charge, with a wooden sword in his hand: he had given his steel one to a disciple who had none. They find him smiling.

effects.log: You carry him all the way to his sect. He weighs almost nothing. You will feel the weight for the rest of your life.
You hang it where you will see it every morning. Some mornings you take it down and do the form.

events.text: The battle of the Descending Gate is won without you. You hear it from a breathless rider: the immortals went back above the clouds, and the alliance holds the pass. Your name is on the list of those who built it, and not on the list of those who stood there at the end.

effects.log: You arrive in time to help bury the dead. It is not nothing.

choices.text: Raise a cup where you are

effects.log: You raise your cup to them alone, and pour it out on the ground. It is the best wine you have, and you wish the day had cost less.

events.text: Under a white banner on the scorched pass, the White Envoy Yun Hwaseol and the alliance's leaders agree a truce: the immortals will not come down uninvited, and the mortal sects will not raise their arrays against the sky. Nobody trusts it. Everybody signs it.

choices.text: Sign it with your own hand

effects.log: Your name is on the truce, below the Envoy's. She glances at it as if memorising it.

choices.text: Ask her about the children taken

effects.log: "They are well," she says. "They are ours now." It is the most honest thing she says all day.

events.text: The truce holds through its first winter. The immortals keep to the clouds. The alliance's sects go back to arguing with each other, which Pyo Mun says is the surest sign that the world is safe again.

effects.log: It feels wonderful.

choices.text: Keep the alliance's arrays ready anyway

effects.log: Just in case. Pyo Mun approves.

events.text: The cloud over the Descending Gate opens, and the light that comes down is not a battle. It is a verdict. By noon the alliance's banners are ash, its arrays are glass, and its names are being read aloud from the sky, one by one, so that the whole world hears them.

effects.log: You hear it, between two names you loved. It sounds strange in heaven's voice.

choices.text: Get the wounded off the mountain

effects.log: You do not listen to the names. You carry people. It is the only thing left to win.

events.text: After the battle the White Envoy comes to your door herself. She does not come for you. She takes someone you love by the hand, kindly, and says they will be an honoured guest above the clouds for as long as you behave. Then they rise into the light, and the door is just a door again.

effects.log: You kneel until the light is gone. You will behave. You will hate every day of it.
The sky does not answer. It did not answer them either.

events.text: The alliance fought at the Descending Gate without you, and lost. You hear it from the survivors on the road: the banners burned, the names read out from the sky. Some of them look at you as they pass. None of them stop.

effects.log: Your house fills with the wounded. Nobody asks where you were. You tell them anyway.
You walk until the road is empty. It does not help.

events.text: You sold the alliance on the night before its battle. By morning its halls are empty, its leaders in chains of light, its banners in the river. Pyo Mun is brought past you on his way up into the clouds. He does not curse you. He only looks, the way one looks at weather.

effects.log: You look away. You will be looking away for the rest of your life.
You hold them until the light takes him. It is the least you owe, and the last.

events.text: The immortals keep their word. The light that takes the alliance's leaders up into the clouds takes you too, gently, on a different road, and something in your dantian opens that was locked for a hundred years. Below, the world you sold grows small, and smaller, and is gone.

effects.log: You keep your eyes on the light. It is very bright. It does not warm you.
You see the Descending Gate, and the river, and a woodcutter's axe standing in the glass. Then only cloud.

events.text: Your hunters fall on the Descending Gate at dawn, and by noon the Mortal Alliance is broken. The cloud halls hold a feast in your name. In the middle of it, Han Biryeo leaves without a word, and his garden of mortal flowers is empty the next morning.

effects.log: The cloud wine is sweet. The toasts are long. Somewhere below, they are reading out names.
His garden is bare earth. He has taken every flower down to the world below, where they will last.

events.text: The mortals hold the Descending Gate. Their arrays drag your hunters out of the sky like nets drag fish, and you come back up through the cloud with your order unfulfilled and your robe in ribbons. The cloud halls will talk about it for a thousand years.

effects.log: The Sovereign hears you out in silence. You are not punished. You are not invited to anything, either.
The Sovereign forbids it. "They have shown us their teeth," he says. "Let them keep them."

events.text: The Sovereign's hunters fall into the trap you warned the mortals of, and the Mortal Alliance wins. In the cloud halls they blame the weather, the mortals' arrays, bad luck. Han Biryeo finds you on the cloud's edge and presses a mortal flower into your hand. It is still alive.

effects.log: You plant it in your own garden. It blooms for a day, and then, for the first time anyone remembers, for a second.
You press it between the pages of a book nobody reads.

events.text: The alliance is crushed, and Lady Ok Seoljin, or someone like her, has given the Sovereign your name. The cloud halls do not punish an immortal openly. They simply stop seeing you: no seat at the feasts, no answer at the doors.

effects.log: He is the only one who still opens his door. He puts the kettle on.
You walk the cloud halls as if they were yours. In a way, now, they are: nobody else will walk beside you.

events.text: A truce is signed on the scorched pass below and sealed in the cloud halls above: the immortals will not come down uninvited, and the mortals will not raise their arrays against the sky. You are one of the few immortals who signs it without holding their nose.

effects.log: Your seal goes on the truce, beside a mortal hand that shook a little.
He brings mortal wine and drinks all of it. It is terrible, he says. You raise your tea.

events.text: Every year on the day of the battle, the people of the province climb to the Descending Gate and tie strips of cloth to the pine that grows from the scorched glass. Children who were not born then tell each other the story wrong.

effects.log: They do not want the true story. It has too much waiting in it. You tell it anyway.

choices.text: Tie your own strip of cloth

effects.log: Yours is plain. Nobody knows it is yours. That suits you.

events.text: The White Envoy comes down once, years after the truce, by invitation, to a sect's festival. She sits at the high table, eats one peach and watches the dancing. On the way out she stops beside you. "It is very loud down here," she says, almost fondly.

choices.text: Say: you get used to it

effects.log: She considers that. "I do not think we would," she says, and goes.
"Grown," she says. "Some ask about you."

events.text: In a mountain village you find a school where children learn the alliance's warding arrays as a game, with chalk, in the dust. The teacher has a scar from the Descending Gate and does not ask yours.

effects.log: They copy it in the dust with great seriousness. Somewhere the alliance is not quite dead.
You leave enough for chalk for a year.

events.text: A blind storyteller in a market sings the ballad of the night the Mortal Alliance was sold. The traitor's name is wrong, and the details are wrong, and the crowd hisses at the traitor exactly where you would.

choices.text: Drop a coin and walk on

effects.log: The storyteller thanks you. You walk faster than you mean to.
The ballad ends with the traitor alone above the clouds. The crowd is satisfied. You are not.

events.text: Years later, the cloud halls still argue about the war with the mortals at every feast. Young immortals who were not there ask what the mortals were like. Everyone looks at you.

effects.log: You tell them about the fires, three thousand of them, like a city. A few of them are very quiet afterwards.
You talk about cranes. Everyone knows what that means now.

events.text: An immortal comes down to buy silk in your town, of all things, and stops dead in the street when you pass. "The Descending Gate," the immortal says, very quietly, as if naming a disease. Then the immortal pays for the silk twice and leaves in a hurry.

effects.log: You do not know why it is funny. Your soul seems to.

choices.text: Follow and ask what was meant

effects.log: The immortal is already a white speck in the sky. The silk merchant gives you the extra coins.

events.text: You dream of a night you have never lived: halls emptying, banners in a river, an old man looking at you the way one looks at weather. You wake with your hands cold and the taste of cloud-wine in your mouth.

choices.text: Light incense for an old man you never met

effects.log: You do not know his name. You light it anyway. It burns straight up.
You will. Mostly. On some nights the old man comes back.

events.text: When white feathers drift down out of a clear sky over the market, everyone looks up in wonder. You alone have your hand on your weapon before you know why.

choices.text: Breathe until your hand lets go

effects.log: It is only feathers. Your hand does not believe it for an hour.
Nothing comes. Something in you is sure it will, one day.

events.text: The cloud halls' archive keeps a record of every soul that ever raised a hand against heaven. A clerk finds yours, turns pale, and goes to fetch someone. When you ask the clerk what it says, the clerk reads out: "Stood at the Descending Gate. Won."

effects.log: The clerk does not smile back. Above the clouds, your past life is not a story. It is a warning.

choices.text: Ask to see the rest of it

effects.log: The clerk will not let you. The Sovereign's steward watches you for the rest of the year.

events.text: An old immortal of the Sovereign's court greets you warmly, as an old friend, and thanks you for a service you do not remember: the night the mortals' alliance was delivered to heaven. The cloud halls remember your soul fondly. You are not sure you want them to.

effects.log: The old immortal pours you cloud-tea. It tastes of a river with banners in it.

choices.text: Say you are not that soul any more

effects.log: "Souls do not change," the old immortal says, kindly. You intend to prove otherwise.

events.text: Han Biryeo's garden is still here, older and wilder, full of mortal flowers that somehow last. A young gardener tends it now. When you walk in, the gardener looks up and says: "He said someone would come back for these."

choices.text: Kneel and help with the weeding

effects.log: You do not remember the garden. Your hands do.
"He went below," the gardener says. "Where the flowers last."
